What You Can Expect
You'll design, implement, and own the inference systems that serve Zoom's AI models at production scale -- across real-time communication, vision, and language workloads. You'll be hands-on with kernel-level optimisation, inference framework internals, and production serving infrastructure, working closely with research and platform teams to push the boundary on latency, throughput, and cost.
About the Team
You will join a dynamic AI Infrastructure team focused on enabling high-performance AI across Zoom's products and services. The team builds the core systems that support model training, deployment, and inference at scale, driving innovation in areas such as real-time communication, computer vision, and natural language understanding.
Responsibilities
Design and build high-performance inference serving systems for large-scale transformer and multimodal models (including 100B+ and MoE architectures)
Implement and tune inference optimisations: speculative decoding, continuous batching, KV cache management, prefill/decode disaggregation, and quantisation (INT4/INT8/FP8)
Contribute to and customise inference frameworks (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang, or equivalent) for Zoom's production requirements
Write and profile CUDA kernels and custom ops where framework-level optimisation is insufficient
Own end-to-end deployment: from model packaging and serving API design to latency SLO monitoring and incident response
Partner with research to translate model architecture changes into inference-efficient implementations
Drive technical design and set the bar for inference engineering practices across the team
What We're Looking For
A Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience
5+ years of software engineering experience, with significant time spent on inference systems or ML infrastructure at production depth
Hands-on experience with at least one major inference framework: vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang, or ONNX Runtime (serving, not just export)
GPU programming experience: CUDA kernel development, memory optimisation, and profiling with Nsight or equivalent tools
Production experience serving LLMs or large vision models -- you've owned latency SLOs, debugged throughput regressions, and shipped optimisations that moved the needle
Depth in at least two of: speculative decoding, continuous batching, KV cache design, quantisation pipelines, prefill/decode disaggregation
Strong systems instincts in Python and C++; ability to read and modify framework internals
Preferred
Advanced degree (Master's or PhD) in a relevant technical field
Experience with MoE models or 100B+ parameter deployments
Familiarity with disaggregated serving architectures or multi-node inference
Background in compiler-level optimisation (XLA, Triton, or similar)

zoom-r19823.text:
The Team
You will join a dynamic AI Infrastructure team focused on enabling high-performance AI across Zoom's products and services. The team builds the core systems that support model training, deployment, and inference at scale, driving innovation in areas such as real-time communication, computer vision, and natural language understanding.
What you can expect
You will build and optimize the inference systems that serve Zoom's AI models in production. Working alongside senior inference engineers, research and platform teams, you will profile serving workloads, find the bottlenecks that limit latency, throughput and cost, and ship the fixes. You will work close to the metal: inside inference frameworks, GPU profiles and serving infrastructure.
Responsibilities
Build, tune and maintain components of Zoom's inference serving stack for transformer and multimodal models, including large and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures
Implement and evaluate inference optimisations such as speculative decoding, continuous batching, KV cache management, parallelism layouts and quantisation (INT4/INT8/FP8)
Extend and customise inference frameworks (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM or equivalent) to support new models and Zoom's production requirements
Profile GPU workloads with Nsight Systems or equivalent tools, root-cause performance regressions, and validate improvements with reproducible benchmarks
Build and improve internal tooling for benchmarking, performance modelling and serving configuration
Partner with researchers to bring new model architectures into production efficiently
Contribute to on-call and production support for the services you build, with guidance from senior engineers
What we're looking for
A degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a related field (MS or PhD preferred), or equivalent practical experience
0–3 years of software engineering experience; internships, research and open-source work in ML systems count
Hands-on experience with at least one inference framework (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM or ONNX Runtime), at the level of serving and modifying it, not only exporting models
Working knowledge of how LLM inference performs on GPUs: memory bandwidth, KV cache, batching, and communication across GPUs
Experience profiling and debugging GPU performance, with evidence of an optimisation you measured and shipped
Depth in at least one of: speculative decoding, continuous batching, KV cache design, quantisation, distributed or multi-GPU serving
Strong programming skills in Python and C++, and comfort reading and changing large framework codebases
Preferred
Merged contributions to vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, PyTorch or similar projects
CUDA, Triton or CUTLASS kernel development
Experience serving MoE or 100B+ parameter models, or multi-node inference (NCCL, RDMA/RoCE)
Graduate coursework or research in ML systems, compilers or high-performance computing

What You Can Expect
At Zoom, we’re building AI that people can trust, and the Trust and Safety Engineering team is central to that mission. As a Machine Learning Engineer, you will develop and enhance AI/ML algorithms and solutions that protect millions of users across the Zoom platform, contributing to a team where your work has immediate impact on user safety. Working alongside experienced researchers and engineers, you will translate cutting-edge research into scalable systems, tackle complex challenges, and continuously grow your technical craft. This is a hybrid position that requires on-site presence 4 days per week at our San Jose, CA office. Remote arrangements are not available for this role.
About the Team
The Trust and Safety Engineering team works to protect Zoom users from abuse and harm, applying state-of-the-art AI and ML to build safer, more trustworthy experiences across the platform. We are a collaborative group of engineers and researchers passionate about translating advanced technology into real-world safety impact, and we take pride in doing that work with rigor and purpose.
Responsibilities
Design, implement, and optimize AI/ML algorithms, techniques, and solutions to address complex Trust and Safety challenges.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate research findings into scalable engineering solutions aligned with business objectives.
Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and technical presentations to uphold the quality and reliability of engineering solutions.
Identify opportunities to improve existing systems and propose innovative solutions that enhance performance, scalability, and reliability.
Stay current with advancements in AI/ML research and engineering, applying emerging knowledge to continuously strengthen our technical capabilities.
What We’re Looking For
5 or more years of professional experience with a Master’s degree or PhD in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related field, or equivalent experience
Proficiency in Python or another relevant programming language
Hands-on experience developing and deploying machine learning models, with solid understanding of ML concepts, algorithms, and techniques; experience with natural language processing (NLP) is a plus
Familiarity with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or similar
Demonstrated enthusiasm for AI through academic or personal projects, with genuine curiosity for emerging possibilities in the field
Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and communicate technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences

What You Can Expect
As a Staff Software Development Engineer on the Onyx team, you'll work at the intersection of enterprise search and generative AI, contributing to a platform that processes millions of queries weekly for organizations like NASA and Hudson River Trading. This is a high-ownership, high-impact role on a small, founder-led team: you'll drive problems from initial discovery through production, with direct visibility into customer outcomes and the open-source community. Working closely with Zoom's AI research and product teams, you'll shape both the technical direction of a growing product and the engineering practices that support it. This position requires on-site presence five (5) days per week at our San Francisco, CA office. Remote or hybrid arrangements are not available for this role.
About the Team
Onyx joined Zoom through acquisition and is building enterprise search and an AI platform for security-conscious organizations. In under three years, the platform grew to hundreds of thousands of users, over one million queries per week, and 30,000 GitHub stars, serving customers including NASA, Hudson River Trading, and Nebius. Our team of roughly a dozen engineers operates across the full product line, from infrastructure and engineering to customer relationships, and works in close collaboration with Zoom's AI research teams on LLMs, classifiers, and embedding models.
Responsibilities
Build capabilities across the Onyx platform that translate advances in NLP and generative AI into reliable, high-value customer experiences.
Solve deep technical challenges in search quality, scalability, and performance at the scale of terabytes of enterprise data.
Own problems from discovery through design, implementation, and production operation, with full accountability for customer outcomes.
Collaborate with Zoom's AI and product teams to develop integrations that amplify value across both product lines and deepen Onyx's competitive position.
Develop fluency across a modern stack (React, Python, Postgres, AWS) and adapt readily to additional technologies as the product evolves.
Shape technical direction and engineering practices as the team and product scale.
Contribute across the full scope of a growing product line, including engineering, infrastructure, rollouts, and exposure to go-to-market initiatives.
What We're Looking For
Demonstrated engineering judgment and deep craft, applied through direct exposure to customers and the open-source community to deliver features that meaningfully improve user experience.
A track record of taking ambiguous problems to reliable solutions with high ownership and substantial, measurable results.
Proficiency with the latest AI development tools, paired with clear opinions on maintaining quality, reliability, and maintainability as engineering practices evolve.
Strong backend engineering experience in complex, data-intensive systems; frontend skills are a plus.
Experience building and operating enterprise software at the reliability, security, and scale demanded by large customers.
Comfort thriving in a fast-moving environment while effectively navigating collaboration across a larger engineering organization.
An appetite for broad contribution across a growing product and business, from core engineering and infrastructure through go-to-market exposure.

What You Can Expect
As an Audio AI Engineer on Zoom's applied research team, you will advance the frontier of audio intelligence by developing and deploying machine-learning models that protect users from synthetic speech and audio deepfakes. Your work will have direct impact on platform trust and security, translating cutting-edge research into robust, production-ready systems. Each day brings a mix of independent experimentation, cross-functional collaboration with research, engineering, product, and security partners, and applied problem-solving at real-world scale. This position requires on-site presence five (5) days per week at our San Jose, California office. Remote or hybrid arrangements are not available for this role.
About the Team
Zoom's AI Research and Engineering team operates at the intersection of innovation and product, building foundational capabilities that power Zoom Workplace experiences for hundreds of millions of users worldwide. The audio AI group is focused on speech intelligence, security, and trust, ensuring that voice and video communications remain authentic and protected as generative technologies evolve. Your contributions here influence the integrity of Zoom's platform and help shape the broader industry conversation around responsible AI.
Responsibilities
Research, design, and develop machine-learning models for audio deepfake and synthetic speech detection.
Design training datasets, evaluation frameworks, and experimental pipelines for audio AI models.
Improve model accuracy and robustness across diverse speakers, languages, devices, codecs, and acoustic environments.
Analyze model failures and engineer solutions for reliable, real-world deployment.
Translate research prototypes into scalable, production-ready systems.
Collaborate cross-functionally with research, engineering, product, and security teams to align on priorities and ship impactful work.
Track and apply emerging developments in speech AI, generative audio, voice cloning, and deepfake detection.
What We're Looking For
PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, Speech/Audio Processing, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Research or industry experience in audio deepfake detection, synthetic speech detection, anti-spoofing, or speaker recognition; experience with generative audio, voice cloning, or adversarial machine learning is a plus.
Strong knowledge of speech and audio signal processing, with familiarity with large-scale or multilingual audio datasets a plus.
Deep understanding of machine learning, deep learning, model evaluation, and experimental design.
Proficiency in Python and deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow; experience deploying and optimizing ML models in production is a plus.
Ability to conduct independent research and translate findings into practical, scalable solutions.
Publications in recognized speech, audio, AI, or machine learning venues are a plus; strong problem-solving, collaboration, and communication skills required.

zoom-r19849.text:
What You Can Expect
In this role, you will design, build, and optimize the data pipelines and analytical solutions that power Zoom’s Online business, including billing, checkout, growth, and revenue analytics. Working end to end, you will own the full data engineering lifecycle, from ETL design and ingestion through data quality, performance tuning, and model delivery to stakeholders across Data Science, Finance, and Product. Each day brings a mix of deep technical work and meaningful cross-functional collaboration, with opportunities to shape how the Online business understands and acts on its data. This is a senior individual contributor role reporting into the Data Systems and Online Technology organization. This is a hybrid position that requires on-site presence three (3) days per week at our Seattle, WA or San Jose, CA office. Remote arrangements are not available for this role.
About the Team
The Online Data team is the analytical backbone of Zoom’s Online business, delivering the data infrastructure and insights that support billing, checkout, growth, and revenue operations. Working alongside Senior Data Engineers, Machine Learning Engineers, and Data Visualization Engineers within the Data Systems and Online Technology organization, our team ensures that decision-makers across Product, Finance, and Data Science have reliable, well-governed data to work from. We build systems and standards that keep Zoom’s Online business moving with confidence.
Responsibilities
Design and implement scalable ETL workflows and data pipelines that transform raw data into structured, analytics-ready formats, with automated validation checks and monitoring to ensure ongoing quality and reliability.
Build analytical datasets from clickstream, user interaction, and product usage events to support web analytics, feature adoption analysis, and user journey insights.
Establish and maintain data governance practices, including data definitions, lineage, ownership documentation, and access controls for sensitive data, in collaboration with cross-functional stakeholders.
Implement automated data quality frameworks covering accuracy, completeness, consistency, and freshness, and establish alerting to identify and resolve data issues proactively.
Optimize pipeline performance and database efficiency through query tuning, indexing strategies, caching configurations, and model accuracy evaluation for large-scale structured and unstructured data.
Analyze complex datasets using statistical techniques and machine learning methods, build interactive visualizations, and run hypothesis testing to surface insights for technical and non-technical audiences.
Lead end-to-end development of data products from concept through deployment, integrating machine learning models into production and providing technical guidance to peers across data engineering and ML workflows.
What We’re Looking For
Data engineering expertise: 8+ years of hands-on experience designing and optimizing complex data pipelines and ETL workflows, including error handling, monitoring, and performance tuning, using tools such as Snowflake, Databricks, Spark, Airflow, dbt, and Python.
SQL and database mastery: Proficiency designing normalized schemas, optimizing complex queries, and applying advanced database features for high-performance analytical workloads.
Machine learning and statistical methods: Experience developing and optimizing ML solutions, designing and executing hypothesis testing strategies, and applying statistical techniques to validate analytical approaches.
Web analytics and product telemetry: Familiarity with event tracking, clickstream data, sessionization, and user identity resolution, with demonstrated experience building analytical datasets from web and product usage data.
Data governance and quality: Experience implementing data standards, metadata management, lineage, ownership, and access controls, combined with the ability to design automated validation tests and anomaly detection to maintain data reliability.
Communication and visualization: Ability to build complex, interactive visualizations and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, with strong skills in independently managing stakeholder relationships.
Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

zoom-r19554.text:
What You Can Expect
As a Lead Staff Site Reliability Engineer, you will be one of the technical leads for our DevOps Platforms organization. This group is responsible for DevOps Platforms including cloud infrastructure, physical data center orchestration, critical security services, and our Zoom for Government (ZfG) environment. You will be an uber tech lead working across a broad area, defining projects and guiding work across various teams. Your scope of work is wide and you will have the opportunity to improve our datacenter kubernetes infrastructure, our cloud infrastructure, our security posture, and our operation of ZfG environments. Broadly speaking, you are an exemplary SRE and you will guide all of our teams toward SRE best practices (automation, monitoring, infrastructure as code, etc).
About the Team
The DevOps Platforms organization owns the full infrastructure stack: cloud infrastructure on AWS and OCI, physical data center orchestration, critical security services (identity, authentication, authorization), and Zoom's FedRAMP-rated federal environment, Zoom for Government (ZfG).
The team is currently working on one of the most technically interesting work in the org, hardening our security posture, and building the automation and reliability systems that underpin Zoom's global services. If you want broad visibility, real cross-team influence, and the chance to define how infrastructure gets built, this is the seat.
Responsibilities
Design and scale DevOps platform services including Kubernetes infrastructure, cloud systems, and compliance-ready environments
Define technical roadmaps and architectural direction for infrastructure automation and security
Partner with service teams to understand platform needs and deliver solutions that improve reliability and efficiency
Establish and advocate for SRE best practices including infrastructure as code, monitoring, and incident management
Mentor team members through design, implementation, and production deployment of complex systems
What We're Looking For
Bring 8+ years of SRE or DevOps experience building and operating production infrastructure at scale
Code proficiently in at least one programming language beyond scripting (e.g., Python, Go, Java)
Deploy and manage CI/CD pipelines using tools like Git, Jenkins, Argo CD, or JFrog
Operate cloud infrastructure on AWS, OCI, or similar platforms using Terraform and Kubernetes
Implement observability solutions with logging and monitoring tools such as ELK, Prometheus, or Grafana

We are seeking a Principal DevOps Engineer who combines deep technical expertise with broad system understanding. This engineer should be capable of diving into a wide range of services and identifying systemic issues across architecture, CI/CD flow, and containerization environments. This role requires technical leadership, analytical skill, and cross-team collaboration to drive reliability, scalability, and modernization.
About the Team
At Zoom, we’re building the next generation of Cloud and Colocation (Colo) infrastructure that powers seamless communication and collaboration for millions of users worldwide.
Responsibilities
Leading deep-dive investigations across diverse services and environments. Working on real time media systems to web, team chat and AI to uncover architectural or operational bottlenecks.
Designing and implementing improvements in deployment pipelines, orchestration frameworks, andCI/CD automation to increase reliability and release velocity.
Working closely with product and service owners to enhance containerization strategy, improve resource efficiency, and reduce operational friction.
Partnering with the Meeting DevOps and Cloud Infra teams to modernize hybrid infrastructures panning colocation data centers, AWS, OCI, and other cloud providers.
Driving system observability, fault isolation, and resilience engineering, ensuring services meet strict availability and latency SLAs.
Providing technical mentorship to DevOps engineers and influence best practices in automation, monitoring, and release engineering. Champion a culture of data-driven reliability through postmortems, SLIs/ SLO's, and continuous performance optimization.
What we’re looking for
15+ years in DevOps, SRE for large-scale, production systems. successful hands-on background in Linux systems, networking, and distributed systems.
Possess experience operating and design low-latency, high-throughput backend services at global scale. Knowledge of media or real-time communication systems (e.g., MMR, WebRTC).
Recognize knowledge of TCP/IP, routing, DNS, load balancing, and packet capture tools. Familiarity with colocation data center operations, including hardware provisioning and troubleshooting.
Demonstrate experience with Terraform, Ansible, Kubernetes, Docker, and modern CI/CD pipelines. successful problem-solving, debugging, and systems-level design skills
Occasional weekend work may be required
Ability to work across the globe or multiple time zones
Mandarin speaking is preferred
